expected_key_facts: Surrender and Renunciation are not two separate additional steps: once you acquire another country's nationality, you surrender your Indian passport and it is stamped 'cancelled due to acquiring foreign nationality' as part of one process.
An Indian passport carrying only a 'cancelled' stamp, without an accompanying certificate, is NOT considered proof that Indian citizenship has been renounced.

When later applying for consular services like a Visa or OCI, you must provide proof of your cancelled Indian passport; if you cannot provide that proof, you will be required to obtain a renunciation certificate.

Depending on whether you still hold your Indian passport, the applicable form is either the Declaration of Surrender of Indian Passport (if you have the passport) or the Declaration of Renunciation of Citizenship of India (if you don't) — these serve the same underlying purpose.
